mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL YoY and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) signals growing demand in the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the interaction effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real final sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and industrial production (INDPRO) also increases, it signals robust demand and supply-side strength, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% MoM and INDPRO increases
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the interaction effect of RSAFS and INDPRO on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle, a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% signals increased liquidity, boosting equity valuations and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during easing cycles.
